name: Hannah
bio:
Hannah was Elkanah's wife, who endured years of taunting from his other wife Peninnah over her childlessness, until she wept and prayed earnestly to the LORD at Shiloh, was granted a son named Samuel, and sang one of the most celebrated prayers in the Old Testament — making her a model of faith rewarded through persistent prayer.

Year after year provoked by Peninnah and deeply distressed, Hannah prayed bitterly at the Shiloh sanctuary, vowing that if the LORD gave her a son, she would dedicate him to the LORD for life, his hair never cut (1 Samuel 1:10-11). The priest Eli, seeing her lips move without sound, mistook her for drunk; Hannah answered, "Not so, my lord... I am a woman who is deeply troubled. I have not been drinking wine or beer; I was pouring out my soul to the LORD," and Eli blessed her, asking God to grant her request (1 Samuel 1:12-18).

The LORD remembered Hannah, and she conceived and bore a son, naming him Samuel, meaning "because I asked the LORD for him" (1 Samuel 1:20). Once the child was weaned, Hannah kept her vow and brought Samuel to Shiloh, giving him to Eli to serve the LORD for life (1 Samuel 1:24-28). Hannah then sang a prayer of awe-filled faith: "My heart rejoices in the LORD... The LORD brings death and makes alive; he brings down to the grave and raises up... He will give strength to his king and exalt the horn of his anointed one" (1 Samuel 2:1-10) — a song whose themes closely echo Mary's Magnificat in the Gospel of Luke. Afterward, the LORD blessed Hannah again, giving her three more sons and two daughters (1 Samuel 2:21). Hannah's story stands as a model of faith that refuses to give up in suffering, and that, once answered, willingly gives back to God what was received.
